title: Economics-driven Preset Editor — proposal and wireframe notes
content:
Purpose:
Short: propose a single editor surface in Optimize that lets infra/ML engineers and product owners author, preview, and validate 'economics-driven presets' — compact bundles of batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that are safe to apply to a model route.
Why: current suggestions are fragmented (separate cards for batching, cache, quantization). Teams want a single place to see cumulative unit-cost impact, latency distribution shifts, and quick simulation before rollout. This will reduce friction for Apply -> Rollout and improve confidence in automated recs.
Audience / Personas: 
- Platform engineer (SRE/infra) — cares about p95, tail latency, SLA impact; will use presets for predictable capacity sizing.
- ML engineer (ops) — cares about quality regressions, per-prompt accuracy and hallucination risk; wants guardrails and fallbacks.
- Product manager / Feature owner — cares about cost and UX changes (latency noticeable to end users); uses economic delta to prioritize.
Key scenarios (user stories):
1) Quick mode: PM opens route, sees a recommended preset with estimated cost delta and latency change; clicks "Preview" to run a 1k-prompt sim and accepts or rejects.
2) Safety-first: ML engineer adjusts quantization profile and toggles aggressive batching; runs regression tests on golden prompts; pins fallback to a float model if quality drop > X%.
3) Programmatic rollout: platform engineer schedules preset for incremental rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback thresholds.
Surface sketch (three-column editor) — high level notes:
- Left column: Preset library and quick filters.
  - List of saved presets (team, org, shared/public). Each row shows small badges: est token cost delta, est latency delta, risk score (low/med/high), last used.
  - Quick actions: clone, compare, delete, export-as-json.
  - Filter facets: workload pattern (latency-sensitive / throughput), model family, target hardware (A100/H100/TPU), author.
- Middle column: Preset composition editor (visual builder).
  - Top bar: preset name, description, visibility (team/org/private), tags.
  - Stacked blocks representing features: Batching block, Caching block, Quantization block, Misc (kv-cache-policy, kv-storage-ttl). Each block is expandable to show knobs.
  - Batching block knobs: target batch size, concurrency cap, adaptiveness slider (static -> adaptive), sequence-length-aware toggles. Tooltip copy for main fields (short UX writing needed).
  - Caching block: prefix caching enabled, prefix window (tokens), reuse threshold, TTL, cold-start warmup tokens. Quick indicator of expected hit-rate (estimate based on historical traces).
  - Quantization block: family presets (int8/q4_0/q4_1/qat), per-layer exceptions (text field / upload list), fallback strategy (re-route to float if quality drop on golden prompts).
  - Right side of middle column: live summary panel that recalculates on change: est tokens/unit, est $/100k tokens, est p95 latency, estimated memory (VRAM) footprint, model compatibility warnings.
- Right column: Simulation & safety checks (sandbox).
  - Run simulation: select prompt cohort (golden set / sampled from recent traffic / custom upload). Options: nPrompts, concurrency pattern, realistic seq length distribution.
  - Output: latency histogram comparison (baseline vs preset), QPS throughput curves, token cost table, and a small quality-delta heatmap (per-prompt metric like log-prob delta or edit distance).
  - Regression alerts: configurable thresholds (e.g., >2% of golden prompts with perplexity increase > X triggers fail).
  - Quick deploy CTA: "Schedule rollout" (opens rollout modal) and a checkbox: "Auto-rollback on regression".
Telemetry & data needs (short list):
- Historical token / prompt distribution by route (seq length percentiles) — used to seed hit-rate and batching sims.
- Per-prompt ground-truth/acceptance metrics for golden set (must be stored lightly in Optimize).
- Kernel/runtime capabilities per host (which quant profiles are supported) — for compatibility warnings.
- Cost model: $/GPU-hour, token compute multipliers by quant profile, per-token egress/storage costs.
Open questions and design tradeoffs (notes to discuss):
- How conservative should the estimator be? (choose optimistic, pessimistic, or configurable bias). Recommendation: default to conservative by applying 10% headroom to latency estimates.
- Should presets mutate route config immediately when applied, or only through rollout steps? Ops preference: only via rollout. Add "applyImmediately" only for sandbox/experiment routes.
- UX for per-layer quant exceptions: free-form vs guided (guided preferred: show top N layers with highest sensitivity and let user toggle).
- Ownership/visibility rules for shared presets — propose team-scoped by default with opt-in org share.
Backlog & next steps (triage for sprint):
- MVP UI tasks: library list + filters (backend API + table), composition editor with 3 blocks (local state only), live summary calc (approx estimator), simulation runner (batch job trigger + basic histogram UI). (JIRA-OPT-893)
- Safety features: golden-prompt upload UI, regression thresholds, auto-rollback flag. (JIRA-OPT-899)
- Integrations: fetch kernel capability matrix from infra catalog, wire cost model into estimator. (CONFLUENCE-OPT-3421)
- UX polish: small-copy tooltips, error states, empty library CTA. (PRD ticket TBD)
- Research spike: evaluate estimator error margin across 10 recent customers to set default headroom. (Spike ticket)
Mockup annotations / copy samples (for designers):
- Batching tooltip title: "Batching profile"; body: "Controls how requests are batched by sequence length and concurrency. Larger batches reduce per-token cost but may increase tail latency."
- Cache badge: "Hit-rate est: 42%" — hover: "Estimated using last 7 days of prefix reuse on this route (sampled)."
- Quantization warning: amber icon with text: "Quantized profile may affect token-level probabilities. Run a golden prompt sim before rollout."
Acceptance criteria for MVP (short):
- Create/Edit preset with batching + caching + quant knobs.
- Run a sandbox sim against a chosen prompt cohort and see latency & cost deltas.
- Schedule a staged rollout with auto-rollback toggled and persistence to DB.
- Integrations: estimator uses historical seq distribution and returns plausible numbers (acceptance: estimator runs within 2s and provides values that product/ops agree are directionally correct).
Notes / loose ideas to explore later:
- Preset diff UI: show overlay comparing two presets (cost/latency/footprint differences).
- CLI-first workflow where presets can be exported/imported via JSON and applied by infra pipelines.
- Marketplace of verified presets (Redwood and partner-certified) with usage metrics and review notes.
- A/B testing harness integrated into rollout modal (easy start/stop and linked metrics).
References and links:
- design: /design/optimize/presets (internal) 
- backend: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-sim-service
- perf notes: slack thread #perf-inference Jan 2026 (thread id 2345)
TODOs (immediate):
- [ ] Schedule 30m scoping with infra to confirm kernel capability API shape (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Draft estimator pseudocode and example outputs for 3 routes (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Quick sketch frames for the three-column layout and sample charts (owner: Maya).
Rough decision log:
- 2025-11-12: team agreed to prefer staged rollouts over immediate apply.
- 2026-01-08: decided to default visibility to team-scoped presets.
- 2026-02-14: added golden-prompt regression threshold requirement for any apply -> rollout pipeline.

(End of doc)
